To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diffusion mechanism of isovalent cation impurities in corundaum weakly depends on impurity ion size.

the vacancy diffusion of isovalent cations in corundum is controlled by two mechanisms, namely migration of cations through interstitials and jumps to nearest aluminum sites at angle to the C-axis; for divalent impurities, the mechanism of vacancy diffusion is changed from monovalent to divalent transport at some concentration of vacancies; and the migration energy of isovalent divalent cations weakly depends on ion size.

Molecular mechanics simulation was employed to study the diffusion mechanism of cation impurity in corundum, and the diffusion energies for different possible paths were obtained by means of the nudged elastic bands method.
